title: 2016 HMMT February Algebra Problem 7
statement:
Determine the smallest positive integer \(n \geq 3\) for which

\[A \equiv 2^{10 n} \quad\left(\bmod 2^{170}\right)\]

where \(A\) denotes the result when the numbers \(2^{10}, 2^{20}, \ldots, 2^{10 n}\) are written in decimal notation and concatenated (for example, if \(n=2\) we have \(A=10241048576\) ).

solutions.text:
Answer: 14
Note that

\[2^{10 n}=1024^{n}=1.024^{n} \times 10^{3 n}\]

So \(2^{10 n}\) has roughly \(3 n+1\) digits for relatively small \(n\) 's. (Actually we have that for \(0<x<1\),

\[(1+x)^{2}=1+2 x+x^{2}<1+3 x\]

Therefore, \(1.024^{2}<1.03^{2}<1.09,1.09^{2}<1.27,1.27^{2}<1.81<2\), and \(2^{2}=4\), so \(1.024^{16}<4\). Thus the conclusion holds for \(n \leq 16\).)
For any positive integer \(n \leq 16\),

\[A=\sum_{i=1}^{n} 2^{10 i} \times 10^{\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(3 j+1)}\]

Let

\[A_{i}=2^{10 i} \times 10^{\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(3 j+1)}\]

for \(1 \leq i \leq n\), then we know that

\[A-2^{10 n}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} A_{i}\]

and

\[A_{i}=2^{10 i+\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(3 j+1)} \times 5^{\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(3 j+1)}=2^{u_{i}} \times 5^{v_{i}}\]

where \(u_{i}=10 i+\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(3 j+1), v_{i}=\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(3 j+1)\). We have that

\[u_{i}-u_{i-1}=10-(3 i+1)=3(3-i)\]

Thus, for \(1 \leq i \leq n-1, u_{i}\) is minimized when \(i=1\) or \(i=n-1\), with \(u_{1}=\frac{3 n^{2}+5 n+12}{2}\) and \(u_{n-1}=13 n-9\). When \(n=5\),

\[A-2^{10 n}=A_{1}+A_{2}+A_{3}+A_{4}=2^{10} \times 10^{46}+2^{20} \times 10^{39}+2^{30} \times 10^{29}+2^{40} \times 10^{16}\]

is at most divisible by \(2^{57}\) instead of \(2^{170}\). For all other \(n\) 's, we have that \(u_{1} \neq u_{n-1}\), so we should have that both \(170 \leq u_{1}\) and \(170 \leq u_{n-1}\). Therefore, since \(170 \leq u_{n-1}\), we have that \(14 \leq n\). We can see that \(u_{1}>170\) and \(14<16\) in this case. Therefore, the minimum of \(n\) is 14 .
